extraction_notes: Supplied public Vishay Siliconix PDF, Document Number 73234, verified SHA-256 56ecdd3176069ea78094a7ffd97192522ac1fdd1b40561c7697bbbeb961bec9b.
Ordering identity is SI2306BDS-T1-E3; the datasheet device title is Si2306BDS and the manufacturer branding is Vishay Siliconix. Manufacturer field follows the supplied identity Vishay Intertech.

The specification headings state TA = 25 degC unless otherwise noted. Curve pages state typical characteristics at 25 degC unless otherwise noted; curve-specific temperature, voltage, current, frequency, and gate-bias conditions are preserved in each curve record.
N-channel polarity is preserved. Tabulated VDS, VGS, ID, IS, and VSD values are represented with the datasheet's positive sign convention; no P-channel magnitude conversion was applied.

Gate-threshold voltage has no typical table entry: MIN is 1.0 V and MAX is 3.0 V at VDS = VGS and ID = 250 uA. The transfer curve is a separate digitized typical characteristic and is not used to invent threshold_typ.

RDS(on) has two published test pairs. Each pair is represented twice to preserve both the TYP and MAX meanings: 0.038 ohm typical and 0.047 ohm maximum at VGS = 10 V, ID = 3.5 A; 0.052 ohm typical and 0.065 ohm maximum at VGS = 4.5 V, ID = 2.8 A. Both are pulse-test values with pulse width <= 300 us and duty cycle <= 2 percent.
Ciss, Coss, and Crss are typical table values converted from pF to SI farads: 305 pF = 3.05e-10 F, 65 pF = 6.5e-11 F, and 29 pF = 2.9e-11 F, at VDS = 15 V, VGS = 0 V, f = 1 MHz.

The body-diode table gives VSD = 0.8 V typical and 1.2 V maximum at IS = 1.25 A and VGS = 0 V. The strict schema has one body_diode field, so the typical value is stored and the maximum is retained here.

The breakdown table gives V(BR)DSS = 30 V minimum at VGS = 0 V and ID = 250 uA. IDSS is 0.5 uA maximum at VDS = 30 V, VGS = 0 V and 10 uA maximum at the same bias with TJ = 55 degC; these quantities are not fields in the strict schema.

Gate charge, gate resistance, switching times, reverse-recovery time and charge, thermal resistance, and absolute maximum ratings are transcribed only in the source PDF because the strict MOSFET extraction schema has no corresponding scalar fields.

Curve points are manual reads from the plotted traces only. The VGS = 5 V through 10 V output family is visibly overlapped and clipped at the 20 A plot limit, so it is not represented as invented individually separated curves.
